title: Plots and reporting
overview_markdown:
**What you will do.** You will turn the results of the association test into plots and tables. You will check that the results are trustworthy. Then you will find the strong signals and write a short report.

**What you will learn.**

- How to draw and read the two main GWAS plots.
- How to check if the test results are too strong overall.
- How to choose a p-value threshold when you run many tests.
- How to group nearby signals and look closely at one region.
- How to report results honestly, including their limits.

**How long it takes.** About 75 minutes. The slowest step is 7.7, because PLINK runs two new association scans.
recap_markdown:
- You drew a QQ plot and calculated an autosomal lambda of approximately 1.016.
- You drew a Manhattan plot. Eight variants are below 5e-8, in three regions on chromosomes 3, 9 and 12.
- You compared thresholds: 5e-8 for the usual rule and approximately 2.11e-7 from Bonferroni for 236,815 tests.
- You grouped the eight variants into three clumps and looked at the L2 region on chromosome 9.
- Without PCs the lambda rose to about 1.546, and without sample or variant QC as well it rose to about 1.655.
- You wrote a final summary and a table of the lead variants.

**Next:** this is the last module of the main path. You can now report your findings, with their limits. Modules A (imputation) and B (mixed models) are optional extras and are not part of the main path.
